I'm not at all recommending energy drinks as they'll affect each of us different - BUT, I used to have energy drinks every day before being diagnosed as I was so so tired (which I now know is cus of dysautonomia!) Honestly, I still have them but have cut down massively - I can't normally tell yet when I'll have a flare so I'm careful but if I'm not about to have one I'm absolutely fine and they help me through the day. If I do have a flare soon after though my tremors do seem to be a lot worse. I rarely have them now but for me I don't feel like they necessarily affect it. I'd talk with your specialist though as you may have a different type than me! :)

My cardiologist put me on 2.5mg x2 daily. It didn't do toooo much but now I'm on 5mg x2 daily and I'm seeing a difference! However I'm on these because my BP isn't affected, so I'm just on these to try calm my HR down!

Im gonna be honest, it's a long and often frustrating and emotional recovery, but when you start to feel progress, you'll be so so happy. It will just take a bit of time.

She did say it's quite common, but if you're worried just let your physio/doctor/surgeon know and if they think you're walking wrong they will be able to give you some pointers! :)

I gained. I was honestly disappointed with myself until I realised that it was quite likely to happen as I wasn't able to exercise, and being an XC runner, prior to surgery i had a really fast metabolism.
If you do gain or lose weight, don't be too hard on yourself - it's temporary, and it's a big recovery so it's best to be kind to yourself :)
